title: Which of these six shapes fold into a cube?
description: Six shapes of six squares each are folded in the mind, one square as the floor, the way the book's solved example folds a net. The board shows two shapes where a square lands on a wall that is already covered, and the four that cover each face once.
teaching_notes: One idea: fold in the mind around one floor square and check that each face gets exactly one square. Watch for students who accept any shape of six squares as a net.

video_script.why: The child decides each shape by folding it in the mind, because a net must cover each of the six faces of the cube once.
video_script.substitution: six shapes of six squares; the shapes with a staircase or a row of four with one square above and one below are nets; the shapes with two extra squares in a column below the row are not.
video_script.anchor: the six shapes of six squares from the book, folded one by one on the stage
video_script.payoff_line: The second, third, fourth and sixth shapes are nets of a cube

final_answer.value: (ii), (iii), (iv) and (vi) are nets of a cube; (i) and (v) are not
final_answer.spoken: the second, third, fourth and sixth shapes are nets of a cube; the first and fifth are not

maths_rules: each shape has 6 squares; a cube has 6 faces
first shape (i): two squares on top of a row of four, joined only at its second square; one extra square is the lid, the other lands on a wall: not a net
second shape (ii): two rows of three joined at one square: folds with no overlap: a net
third shape (iii): staircase of 2, 2 and 2 squares: a net
fourth (iv) and sixth (vi): a row of four with one square above and one below: the extra squares are the lid and the bottom: nets
fifth shape (v): two squares hanging in a column below the second square of a row of four; one is the bottom, the other lands on a wall, the lid is missing: not a net
4 nets and 2 shapes that are not nets make 6 shapes
video_script.design: One idea: fold in the mind around one floor square. Each square is tinted with the face it lands on; a doubled face and an empty face glow in the warning colour.
open_questions: The six shapes of the book are figures that the extracted text does not show; they are described as in the worklist.
